content: Prosopis is a genus that includes approximately 45 species of leguminous, spiny trees and shrubs. These plants are distributed across subtropical and tropical regions of the Americas, Africa, and Southwest Asia. They are well-adapted to arid environments, often thriving in dry soils and demonstrating significant drought resistance. In some cases, they develop extremely deep root systems to access water. The wood of Prosopis species is characteristically hard, dense, and durable. Their fruits are pod-like structures, which can contain substantial amounts of sugar. Species Some notable species within the Prosopis genus include: Mesquite species (found in the southern United States and Mexico): Prosopis glandulosa (commonly known as Honey Mesquite) Prosopis pallida Prosopis pubescens (known as Screwbean Mesquite) Prosopis reptans (referred to as Tornillo) Prosopis strombulifera (Creeping Mesquite) Prosopis velutina (Velvet Mesquite) South American species (commonly referred to as algarrobos, found in the Gran Chaco and other regions): Prosopis affinis (Ñandubay) Prosopis alba (Algarrobo blanco) Prosopis alba var. panta (Algarrobo panta) Prosopis caldenia (Caldén) Prosopis chilensis (Algarrobo chileno) Prosopis fiebrigii Prosopis flexuosa (Alpataco) Prosopis hassleri Prosopis juliflora Prosopis kuntzei (Itín) Prosopis nigra (Algarrobo negro) Prosopis rojasiana Prosopis ruscifolia (Vinal) African species: Prosopis africana Asian species (found in regions such as India, particularly Rajasthan, as well as Syria and Iraq): Prosopis cineraria (known by various names such as Khejri, Jand, Sangri, and Kandi) Phytochemistry The genus Prosopis has been found to contain several bioactive compounds, including: 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin) Apigenin Isorhamnetin-3-diglucoside L-arabinose Quercetin Tannins Tryptamine These phytochemical constituents suggest potential pharmacological and therapeutic applications for Prosopis species.
